findings.highlight: driving away evil spirits is not a priest’s duty
findings.evidenceJa: 悪霊払いは神父の生業、というのは間違いである
findings.governingReading: The opening says it is mistaken to call exorcism a priest’s occupation or livelihood.
findings.explanation: The English narrows an assertion about what priests do as an occupation into what their duty requires.

findings.highlight: Supreme and all-knowing
findings.evidenceJa: 至高にして全なるもの
findings.governingReading: Their God is supreme and whole or all-encompassing.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes omniscience for totality.

findings.highlight: A spirit that created the perfect world.
findings.evidenceJa: 完璧な世界を作り上げた聖霊だ
findings.governingReading: The passage calls God the Holy Spirit that fashioned a perfect world.
findings.explanation: The English lowercases and genericizes the Holy Spirit as merely “a spirit.”

findings.highlight: Such a god would never allow evil to disgrace the world that he created.
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの子である人を穢し、自らが創造した世界を汚す魔などを容認する道理がない
findings.governingReading: There is no reason God would tolerate demons that defile humans, his own children, and pollute the world he created.
findings.explanation: The English omits humans as God’s children and the distinct corruption of humanity.

findings.highlight: a necessary part of the world. It is something worthy of love
findings.evidenceJa: 主が構築した世界に必要な欠片、愛すべき被造物
findings.governingReading: Even threatening demons are necessary pieces of the Lord’s constructed world and created beings worthy of love.
findings.explanation: The English omits their explicit status as created beings and loosens the Lord’s authorship.

findings.highlight: If what brings out the goodness of men is holy, it follows that what brings out the malice of men is evil
findings.evidenceJa: 人の善性を鍛えるものが聖ならば、人の悪性を鍛えるものが魔
findings.governingReading: If the holy trains human goodness, demons correspondingly train human evil.
findings.explanation: The English changes active moral tempering or training into merely bringing traits out.

findings.highlight: producing gruesome tragedies
findings.evidenceJa: 凄惨な悲劇喜劇を演出する
findings.governingReading: Demons stage gruesome tragedies and comedies beyond human understanding.
findings.explanation: The English deletes “comedies,” removing the grotesque paired formulation.

findings.highlight: made people realize how powerless God is
findings.evidenceJa: 人の子に天の無力さを錯覚させた
findings.governingReading: Heaven’s designs sometimes caused humanity to mistake Heaven for powerless.
findings.explanation: The English promotes an explicitly false impression into realized fact and changes Heaven into God.

findings.highlight: Apostles, humans that carry out the will of God
findings.evidenceJa: 主の代行を成す使徒が赦された
findings.governingReading: Messengers who act as the Lord’s proxies were permitted despite being human.
findings.explanation: The English uses “Apostles,” a loaded Nasu term, and omits the explicit proxy function and exceptional permission.

findings.highlight: They drive away darkness
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは魔を払い
findings.governingReading: Executors expel demons or magical evils.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete supernatural target with abstract darkness.

findings.highlight: adaptable as the snake
findings.evidenceJa: 蛇の如き移り身
findings.governingReading: Assassin mocks the Church for teaching snake-like shifting or changeability.
findings.explanation: The English makes the charged accusation into positive adaptability.

findings.highlight: The white skull laughs
findings.evidenceJa: 白い髑髏が嘲笑う
findings.governingReading: Assassin, figured through his white skull mask, sneers.
findings.explanation: The English again presents the mask as a literal skull and weakens 嘲笑う to laughter.

findings.highlight: a Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: 令呪が数個
findings.governingReading: Kirei retains several still-powered Command Spells unused since the previous war.
findings.explanation: The English reduces several Command Spells to one.

findings.highlight: the selected Agents
findings.evidenceJa: 選ばれた代行者
findings.governingReading: The comparison invokes the Scripture-class armament said to be held by chosen Executors.
findings.explanation: The English switches established terminology from “Executors” to the generic “Agents.”

findings.highlight: the mad warrior crashing into the distance
findings.evidenceJa: 遠退いていく狂戦士の足音
findings.governingReading: Kirei listens to the footsteps of Berserker receding into the distance.
findings.explanation: The English changes footsteps into crashing and makes the manner of movement explicit.

findings.highlight: You could have used the boy as bait to escape
findings.evidenceJa: 以前のおぬしならば小僧を撒き餌にしても逃げ切ろう
findings.governingReading: Zouken says the Kirei of old would have escaped even if it meant using Shirou as bait.
findings.explanation: The English removes the comparison with Kirei’s former character and makes it a mere available tactic.

findings.highlight: Do not tell me you are moved by kindness
findings.evidenceJa: よもや情に絆された
findings.governingReading: Zouken asks whether Kirei has improbably been bound or swayed by human feeling.
findings.explanation: The English narrows 情 to kindness, losing the taunt about emotional attachment itself.

findings.highlight: he speaks with no sign of hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 見えざる老魔術師に言い放った
findings.governingReading: Kirei declares this to the unseen old magus without even kindling killing intent.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unseen addressee from the speech frame.

findings.highlight: with no sign of hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 殺気すら灯さず
findings.governingReading: Kirei speaks without even lighting murderous intent.
findings.explanation: The English weakens killing intent to hostility and loses the ignition metaphor.

findings.highlight: I know we will both die eventually
findings.evidenceJa: じき殺されるのは判っている
findings.governingReading: Kirei knows that he and Shirou will shortly be killed.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the imminence and the external killer.

findings.highlight: do something for yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 己が目的の為に手を打つ
findings.governingReading: Before death, it is natural to take action for one’s own objective.
findings.explanation: The English turns pursuit of a specific objective into generic self-serving action.

findings.highlight: Thenit is only natural
findings.evidenceJa: ならば死ぬ前に
findings.governingReading: Then it is natural to act before dying.
findings.explanation: The English joins “Then” and “it” into malformed prose.

findings.highlight: I can do nothing, even if I defeat Assassin here and move to help the boy
findings.evidenceJa: 助けに行ったところで間に合わん
findings.governingReading: Even if Kirei defeats Assassin and goes to help, he will not arrive in time.
findings.explanation: The English changes lateness into unspecified inability to do anything.

findings.highlight: melts into the forest without trace
findings.evidenceJa: 木々に擬態し、その姿を完全に消失させ
findings.governingReading: The white mask camouflages itself among the trees and completely vanishes from view.
findings.explanation: The English changes deliberate camouflage into melting.

findings.highlight: The sword held by the priest
findings.evidenceJa: 神父の穿つ剣
findings.governingReading: The priest drives or pierces with his blade against Assassin’s thrown dagger.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the blade’s attacking action with static possession.

findings.highlight: I shall see through the battle of the Church’s outlier
findings.evidenceJa: 何処まで戦うか見届けて進ぜようぞ
findings.governingReading: Zouken grandly offers to watch how far the Church outlier can fight.
findings.explanation: The English omits the question of Kirei’s limit and produces the unnatural phrase “see through the battle.”

findings.highlight: Malak al-Maut
findings.evidenceJa: 老魔術師の操る死の天使
findings.governingReading: The narration calls Assassin the angel of death controlled by the old magus.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a specific Arabic name absent from the Japanese, changing the cultural register.

findings.highlight: run fasterrun fast like Kotomine
findings.evidenceJa: もっと速く言峰のように速く走って
findings.governingReading: Shirou must run faster—fast like Kotomine.
findings.explanation: The English splices two phrases into “fasterrun.”

findings.highlight: my bones are screaming to break
findings.evidenceJa: 股から骨がブチ折れるぞと悲鳴をあげている
findings.governingReading: His leg muscles are tearing and the bones scream that they will snap from the crotch or hip.
findings.explanation: The English omits where the breaking sensation begins and leaves the bones “screaming to break” in awkward English.

findings.highlight: I’ve covered five kilometers already
findings.evidenceJa: 五キロはとっくに走った
findings.governingReading: Shirou believes he passed five kilometers long ago.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a distance well beyond five kilometers to five kilometers completed.

findings.highlight: I’m so short of breath that I can’t think
findings.evidenceJa: 酸欠で回らない頭
findings.governingReading: His oxygen-starved brain is not functioning properly.
findings.explanation: The English replaces cerebral oxygen deprivation with being short of breath.

findings.highlight: I ran full speed without slowing down
findings.evidenceJa: これでもかと走り続けた
findings.governingReading: He kept running with everything he could possibly give, at full speed without easing pace.
findings.explanation: The English omits the insistence that he has pushed the effort to its utter limit.

findings.highlight: But it won’t go away
findings.evidenceJa: だというのに離れない
findings.governingReading: Despite all his running, the distance between them will not open.
findings.explanation: The English leaves an unclear “it” that merely will not go away.

findings.highlight: my heart and muscles are about to stop
findings.evidenceJa: 心筋が硬直し停止しようとしている
findings.governingReading: His cardiac muscle is stiffening and trying to stop.
findings.explanation: The English splits one anatomical subject into his heart and all his muscles.

findings.highlight: the presence behind me is getting larger
findings.evidenceJa: 気配は容赦なく強大になっていく
findings.governingReading: The pursuing presence is mercilessly becoming more powerful or overwhelming.
findings.explanation: The English turns increasing force into physical size and omits mercilessness.

findings.highlight: Run so I won’t think negative thoughts
findings.evidenceJa: つまらない弱音が真っ白になるまで走れ
findings.governingReading: Run until his petty weak complaints are bleached completely blank.
findings.explanation: The English changes the erasure of articulated weakness into avoiding negative thoughts.

findings.highlight: My mind reacts to her frantic warning before my body does
findings.evidenceJa: 心より速く体が反応した
findings.governingReading: His body reacts to Illya’s whole-hearted warning faster than his conscious mind or heart.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the order, making mind react before body.

findings.highlight: her frantic warning
findings.evidenceJa: 全身全霊をこめた忠告
findings.governingReading: Illya puts her entire body and soul into the warning.
findings.explanation: The English reduces total commitment to frantic delivery.

findings.highlight: My feet slide to a halt in the dirt
findings.evidenceJa: 土を抉りながら体を止め
findings.governingReading: Shirou arrests his body while gouging up the earth.
findings.explanation: The English turns a forceful earth-gouging stop into feet sliding in dirt.

findings.highlight: the sword I had on my waist
findings.evidenceJa: 腰に下げていた黒鍵
findings.governingReading: Shirou readies the Black Key hanging at his waist.
findings.explanation: The English discards the established weapon name.

findings.highlight: create a Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路を発現させる
findings.governingReading: Shirou manifests or activates his magical circuits at an imagined two hundred miles per hour.
findings.explanation: The English changes plural circuit activation into creating one circuit.

findings.highlight: In an instant, I manufacture everything without even thinking about it.
findings.evidenceJa: その全てを頭に浮かべず、同時に、一瞬で工程を通過した
findings.governingReading: Nothing whatsoever enters Shirou’s mind; without consciously picturing any of it, he traverses every process simultaneously in an instant.
findings.explanation: The English says he manufactures everything, reversing absence of mental objects into creation and obscuring the simultaneous procedural compression.

findings.highlight: I resist the impact with all my strength
findings.evidenceJa: 両手で、満身の力でその一撃に抵抗した
findings.governingReading: Shirou resists the single blow with both hands and all his strength.
findings.explanation: The English omits the two-handed physical stance.

findings.highlight: All it took was one blow.
findings.evidenceJa: わずか一撃で粉砕された
findings.governingReading: His body bursts or is flung away, rhetorically pulverized by just one blow.
findings.explanation: The English preserves flight but leaves “all it took” without stating the pulverization it took one blow to accomplish.

findings.highlight: permeating damage from the tip of my head to my toes
findings.evidenceJa: 衝撃は両腕から全身に駆け上がり
findings.governingReading: The transmitted shock races from both arms through his whole body and penetrates from crown to toes.
findings.explanation: The English changes the traveling shock into unspecified damage and omits its origin in both arms.

findings.highlight: The attack I made with all my might
findings.evidenceJa: 全身全霊、全てを篭めて対抗した一撃
findings.governingReading: The blow with which Shirou resisted contains his whole body, soul, and everything he has.
findings.explanation: The English calls it his attack and compresses the total embodied resistance into “all my might.”

findings.highlight: was deflected like nothing
findings.evidenceJa: 一方的に粉砕された
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s utmost resistance is one-sidedly pulverized.
findings.explanation: The English changes destruction into casual deflection.

findings.highlight: Escape is impossible.
findings.evidenceJa: 逃走は絶望的だった
findings.governingReading: The difference in force makes escape hopeless.
findings.explanation: The English promotes practical hopelessness into categorical impossibility.

findings.highlight: I accept my fate, but
findings.evidenceJa: 受け入れそうになった時
findings.governingReading: Shirou is on the verge of accepting unavoidable death when seeing Illya interrupts him.
findings.explanation: The English says he accepts it, erasing the incomplete threshold that Illya prevents him from crossing.

findings.highlight: Illya crying in disbelief
findings.evidenceJa: 愕然と涙するイリヤ
findings.governingReading: Illya is stunned or aghast and crying before the black enemy.
findings.explanation: The English retains disbelief but weakens her shocked collapse.

findings.highlight: I frantically reach out
findings.evidenceJa: 咄嗟に腕を伸ばす
findings.governingReading: Shirou reflexively or instantly reaches out.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes emotional franticness for reflexive timing.

findings.highlight: it feels like I’ll explode if I take another
findings.evidenceJa: その一息だけで体がパン、と風船みたいに破裂しそう
findings.governingReading: Although starved for oxygen, even that one possible breath makes his body feel ready to pop like a balloon.
findings.explanation: The English invents a second breath and makes it the condition of explosion, reversing the paradox.

findings.highlight: That single breath gives me the strength to run
findings.evidenceJa: 一息分の呼吸があれば地面を蹴れる
findings.governingReading: One breath is enough for Shirou to kick off the ground.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes a concrete single push from the earth into strength for continued running.

findings.highlight: I use all of my Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術回路を総動員し
findings.governingReading: Shirou mobilizes all of his magical circuits.
findings.explanation: The English uses an ungrammatical singular “all of my Magic Circuit.”

findings.highlight: His body is covered by the black mud
findings.evidenceJa: 全身は黒い泥に侵食され
findings.governingReading: Berserker’s whole body is being eroded or invaded by black mud.
findings.explanation: The English turns active corruption into surface covering.

findings.highlight: His glowing, red eyes are there to emit hostility
findings.evidenceJa: 赤く光る両目は殺気を放つだけ
findings.governingReading: The red glowing eyes serve only to emit killing intent, not sight.
findings.explanation: The English weakens killing intent into hostility.

findings.highlight: Engulfed in the mud
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い影に呑まれ
findings.governingReading: Berserker has been swallowed by the black shadow.
findings.explanation: The English changes the consuming entity from the shadow to mud.

findings.highlight: can’t recognize Illya’s figure, let alone mine
findings.evidenceJa: 眼球には、俺は勿論、イリヤの姿さえ映っておらず
findings.governingReading: Neither Shirou nor even Illya’s image is reflected in Berserker’s eyeballs.
findings.explanation: The English changes a physical absence of visual registration into cognitive failure to recognize them.

findings.highlight: He raises his axe-sword
findings.evidenceJa: 咆哮と共に
findings.governingReading: Berserker raises the axe-sword with a roar.
findings.explanation: The English omits the roar accompanying the action.

findings.highlight: The priest is about to end his life.
findings.evidenceJa: 神父は最期の時を迎えた
findings.governingReading: The narration presents the priest as having reached his final moment.
findings.explanation: “End his life” suggests deliberate suicide rather than apparent imminent death at an enemy’s hands.

findings.highlight: the white skull
findings.evidenceJa: 前方にかすむ髑髏
findings.governingReading: Kirei stares at the skull shape dimly visible ahead.
findings.explanation: The English supplies whiteness and omits its indistinct appearance.

findings.highlight: His outfit is slashed up.
findings.evidenceJa: 存分に切り刻まれた神父服
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s priestly vestments have been thoroughly cut to ribbons.
findings.explanation: The English genericizes the clerical clothing and weakens the extent of damage.

findings.highlight: lasting this long against a Servant
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを向こうによく保った
findings.governingReading: Zouken mockingly commends Kirei for keeping the Servant held away for so long.
findings.explanation: The English changes maintenance of separation into merely surviving a duration against Assassin.

findings.highlight: The old man’s laugh echoes through the sky.
findings.evidenceJa: 老人の哄笑が空を覆う
findings.governingReading: The old man’s guffaw covers the sky.
findings.explanation: The English replaces an engulfing spatial image with ordinary echo.

findings.highlight: weapons to measure the strength of his opponent
findings.evidenceJa: 急所を狙う短刀は、同時に獲物の能力を測る物差しでもある
findings.governingReading: The daggers aimed lethally at vital points also serve as rulers measuring the prey’s capabilities.
findings.explanation: The English drops the ruler metaphor and the simultaneous lethal targeting, while narrowing capability to strength.

findings.highlight: a distance at which only projectile weapons are useful
findings.evidenceJa: 投擲武器でしか届かない間合い
findings.governingReading: Assassin maintains a range reachable only by thrown weapons.
findings.explanation: The English changes physical reach into the broader claim that only projectile weapons are useful.

findings.highlight: He will drive them into a corner by cutting their limbs and tiring their bodies.
findings.evidenceJa: 心臓を破裂寸前まで追い込んでいく
findings.governingReading: Assassin drives the body as far as the brink of cardiac rupture.
findings.explanation: The English omits the culminating physiological pressure entirely.

findings.highlight: his evil arm
findings.evidenceJa: 魔の腕
findings.governingReading: Assassin brings down his supernatural or demonic arm.
findings.explanation: The English moralizes the arm as evil.

findings.highlight: It’s just a chore for Assassin, bringing him no joy.
findings.evidenceJa: 何の愉しみもない日常だった
findings.governingReading: This joyless procedure is Assassin’s ordinary daily routine.
findings.explanation: The English retains joyless work but omits how normal and habitual it is for him.

findings.highlight: at least twenty
findings.evidenceJa: 二十を超える
findings.governingReading: Assassin has used more than twenty daggers.
findings.explanation: “At least twenty” includes exactly twenty and weakens the strict lower bound.

findings.highlight: The priest has blocked them and reached this ruin.
findings.evidenceJa: それを凌ぎながら森を抜け、この廃墟に辿り着いた
findings.governingReading: While surviving every lethal throw, Kirei passed through the forest and reached the ruin.
findings.explanation: The English omits his traversal out of the forest.

findings.highlight: The seven he threw were all dodged.
findings.evidenceJa: 弾丸の如く放った七本の黒鍵は、悉くがアサシンに躱され、何処かに消えていった
findings.governingReading: All seven Black Keys fired like bullets were evaded and vanished somewhere beyond the fight.
findings.explanation: The English omits their bullet-like speed and disappearance, both of which explain why only three remain.

findings.highlight: Show him some grace
findings.evidenceJa: 慈悲をくれてやるがよい
findings.governingReading: Zouken tells Assassin to bestow mercy, in context meaning the finishing blow.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes social grace for mercy.

findings.highlight: the temple, pancreas, and diaphragm
findings.evidenceJa: 眉間膵臓横隔膜
findings.governingReading: The three simultaneous targets are the point between the eyebrows, the pancreas, and the diaphragm.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the first target to the temple.

findings.highlight: the lightning flashes
findings.evidenceJa: まったく同時、一息で放たれた紫電
findings.governingReading: Three purple-lightning throws are released in one breath at exactly the same instant.
findings.explanation: The English omits their simultaneity, single-breath execution, and purple color.

findings.highlight: There is a term called “fatal attack.”
findings.evidenceJa: 必至、という言葉がある
findings.governingReading: The narration invokes 必至: a forced, inescapable winning sequence in which the next move certainly kills.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the technical tactical concept to the generic phrase “fatal attack.”

findings.highlight: the one-winged spear, is developed
findings.evidenceJa: 片翼の槍が展開される
findings.governingReading: The long cursed arm unfolds or deploys as a one-winged spear.
findings.explanation: The English uses the unnatural and mechanically inaccurate “is developed.”

findings.highlight: his prey is tired and wounded
findings.evidenceJa: 疲労し出血した獲物
findings.governingReading: Assassin has measured prey that is exhausted and actively bleeding.
findings.explanation: The English replaces active blood loss with generic injury.

findings.highlight: only three meters
findings.evidenceJa: わずか二間
findings.governingReading: Kirei can jump only two ken sideways, approximately 3.6 meters.
findings.explanation: The English shortens the distance to three meters without indicating approximation.

findings.highlight: Set
findings.evidenceJa: 告げる
findings.governingReading: Kirei begins the formula with “I declare.”
findings.explanation: The English substitutes “Set,” obscuring the liturgical declaration.

findings.highlight: aim for is a double-kill
findings.evidenceJa: この身を捨てての相打ち狙い
findings.governingReading: His sole remaining method is to throw away his own body and seek a mutual strike.
findings.explanation: The English presents a double kill as the objective while omitting bodily self-sacrifice and the exchange-of-blows logic.

findings.highlight: The Black Keys will certainly hit him.
findings.evidenceJa: この体勢で放てば黒鍵は命中する
findings.governingReading: The Black Keys will hit if released from this posture.
findings.explanation: The English removes the condition supplied by Kirei’s particular position.

findings.highlight: The three swords will pierce through Assassin, sticking to the tree behind him.
findings.evidenceJa: 三本の剣はアサシンを貫通し、背後の幹に縫い付ける
findings.governingReading: The three blades will pierce Assassin and sew or pin him to the trunk behind him.
findings.explanation: The English’s “sticking to the tree” is grammatically unclear and weakens deliberate immobilization.

findings.highlight: The inhuman action is like a cannon firing.
findings.evidenceJa: 冗談じみた上昇は、砲台の弾丸そのものだった
findings.governingReading: The absurd ascent is the very image of a cannon projectile.
findings.explanation: The English changes comic impossibility into inhumanity and compares the action to firing rather than Kirei to the projectile.

findings.highlight: Amassing his strength and releasing it
findings.evidenceJa: 力を溜めに溜め、限界まで引き絞った筋肉を解放し
findings.governingReading: Kirei releases muscles in which he has accumulated force upon force and drawn them to their absolute limit.
findings.explanation: The English omits the repeated accumulation and bow-like drawing of his muscles to their limit.

findings.highlight: Matou Zouken, the one who has been observing the battle
findings.evidenceJa: 神父の処刑を愉しんでいた間桐臓硯
findings.governingReading: Zouken has been enjoying what he believes is the priest’s execution.
findings.explanation: The English turns sadistic enjoyment and presumed execution into neutral observation.

findings.highlight: HmWhat are you doing, Assassin
findings.evidenceJa: ぬア、アサシン、何をしておるか
findings.governingReading: Zouken cries out and demands what Assassin is doing.
findings.explanation: The English joins the cry and question into malformed “HmWhat.”

findings.highlight: This has always been his announced intention.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼の狙いは初めからソレだけだと言っていた
findings.governingReading: Kirei had said from the beginning that this alone was his target.
findings.explanation: The English omits exclusivity and leaves the referent of “this” less concrete.

findings.highlight: slams his head against the wall
findings.evidenceJa: 頭部を鷲掴みにしたまま壁に叩きつけ
findings.governingReading: Still clutching Zouken’s head in an eagle grip, Kirei slams the body into the wall.
findings.explanation: The English omits the continuous one-handed grip that controls the destruction.

findings.highlight: HaI see, so you will kill me
findings.evidenceJa: はそうか、ワシを殺すか
findings.governingReading: Zouken begins with a broken laugh or gasp before saying he understands.
findings.explanation: The English fuses “Ha” and “I” into malformed text.

findings.highlight: Leaving a smear of blood across the stones
findings.evidenceJa: 壁に血の跡を残しながら
findings.governingReading: Kirei walks while leaving a trail of blood on the wall.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the wall with unspecified stones and a continuous smear, weakening the setup for the wall-as-file image.

findings.highlight: The blood and flesh paint a picture on the wall.
findings.evidenceJa: 壁に描かれていく血の跡肉の跡
findings.governingReading: Trails of blood and flesh are progressively drawn across the wall.
findings.explanation: The English invents a coherent “picture” rather than tracks produced by abrasion.

findings.highlight: His body has been ground away against the stone.
findings.evidenceJa: 壁という鑢に摩り下ろされた
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s body is grated down by the wall as though the wall itself were a file.
findings.explanation: The English preserves grinding but omits the file metaphor and changes wall to stone.

findings.highlight: Ask for forgiveness here.
findings.evidenceJa: 許しはここに
findings.governingReading: Forgiveness is here.
findings.explanation: The English turns a declaration of present forgiveness into an imperative to request it.

findings.highlight: Kyrie eleison.
findings.evidenceJa: この魂に憐れみを
findings.governingReading: The displayed plea asks for mercy upon this soul while the ruby supplies the liturgical Kyrie eleison.
findings.explanation: The English retains only the liturgical phrase and loses the soul-specific written meaning.

findings.highlight: The laughter is cut off.
findings.evidenceJa: 消えていく哄笑
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s guffaw fades away.
findings.explanation: The English makes gradual disappearance an abrupt cutoff.

findings.highlight: The shape that can’t be seen by human eyes withers away.
findings.evidenceJa: 目には見えぬ重み、人の眼には映されないカタチが薄れていく
findings.governingReading: An invisible weight and a form human eyes cannot perceive grow faint.
findings.explanation: The English omits the invisible weight and changes fading into withering.

findings.highlight: the systematic basis of their magic
findings.evidenceJa: 世界に固定化された魔術基盤
findings.governingReading: The Church’s teaching is a magical foundation fixed into the world, described as among the greatest anti-spirit magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English turns an ontologically world-fixed magical foundation into the vague “systematic basis of their magic.”

findings.highlight: the greatest weapon against spirits
findings.evidenceJa: 最大の対霊魔術
findings.governingReading: It is regarded as the highest or greatest class of anti-spirit magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English changes a technical classification of magecraft into a generic weapon.

findings.highlight: wandering souls
findings.evidenceJa: 肉の身より離れ、腐り狂いながらも世に迷う魂
findings.governingReading: The rite concerns a soul separated from flesh that wanders the world while rotting and maddened.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the separation from flesh and the soul’s corruption and madness.

findings.highlight: eliminates
findings.evidenceJa: 無に還す
findings.governingReading: The providential key returns the wandering soul to nothingness.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the cosmological destination to elimination.

findings.highlight: the wish of the five hundred-year-old magus
findings.evidenceJa: 五百年を生きた老魔術師の妄念
findings.governingReading: The rite sublimates the obsessive delusion or fixation of the old magus who lived five hundred years.
findings.explanation: The English makes his five-century life his age and sanitizes 妄念 into an ordinary wish.
